html:
On 9 August 1965 Singapore left Malaysia and became an independent republic, two years after it had joined.

The merger had gone badly. Lee Kuan Yew's People's Action Party called for a Malaysian Malaysia with equal rights for all races, while leaders in Kuala Lumpur defended special rights for Malays. Race riots broke out in Singapore in 1964. Prime Minister Tunku Abdul Rahman decided that Singapore must go.

Lee wept on television as he announced it. With no hinterland, no water of its own and no army, the city-state built its future on trade, the port, foreign investment and public housing.
sum: On 9 August 1965 Singapore left Malaysia and became an independent republic, two years after it had joined.
